title.raw: 《東越列傳》 Treatise on the Eastern Yue

sentences.zh: 閩越王無諸及越東海王搖者，其先皆越王句踐之後也，姓騶氏。

translations.literal: The King of Minyue, Wuzhu, and the King of the Eastern Sea Yue, Yao, were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue, and bore the surname Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu, the King of Minyue, and Yao, the King of Eastern Sea Yue, were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue and bore the clan name Zou.

sentences.zh: 秦已并天下，皆廢為君長，以其地為閩中郡。

translations.literal: After Qin had unified the realm, it deposed them all to the status of chieftains and made their territory the Commandery of Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin dynasty united the realm, it stripped them of their royal titles, reducing them to local chieftains, and incorporated their territory into the Commandery of Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 及諸侯畔秦，無諸、搖率越歸鄱陽令吳芮，所謂鄱君者也，從諸侯滅秦。

translations.literal: When the feudal lords rebelled against Qin, Wuzhu and Yao led the Yue people to submit to the magistrate of Poyang, Wu Rui—the one known as Lord Po—and joined the feudal lords in overthrowing Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the lords rose against Qin, Wuzhu and Yao led their Yue followers to join Wu Rui, the magistrate of Poyang—known as Lord Po—and fought alongside the other lords to bring down the Qin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，項籍主命，弗王，以故不附楚。

translations.literal: At that time, Xiang Ji held the power to grant titles and did not make them kings, so they did not attach themselves to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Xiang Yu held the power to bestow titles but did not make them kings, and so they never aligned themselves with Chu.

sentences.zh: 漢擊項籍，無諸、搖率越人佐漢。

translations.literal: When Han attacked Xiang Ji, Wuzhu and Yao led the Yue people to assist Han.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han forces campaigned against Xiang Yu, Wuzhu and Yao led their Yue warriors to fight on the side of Han.

sentences.zh: 漢五年，復立無諸為閩越王，王閩中故地，都東冶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Han, Wuzhu was again established as the King of Minyue, ruling over the former territory of Minzhong, with his capital at Dongye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Han dynasty, Wuzhu was restored as the King of Minyue, reigning over the old Minzhong territory from his capital at Dongye.

sentences.zh: 孝惠三年，舉高帝時越功，曰閩君搖功多，其民便附，乃立搖為東海王，都東甌，世俗號為東甌王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Xiaohui, reviewing the merits of the Yue from the time of Emperor Gao, it was said that Lord Yao of Min had rendered great service and his people readily submitted to him, so Yao was established as the King of the Eastern Sea, with his capital at Dong'ou; the common people called him the King of Dong'ou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Hui's reign, the court reviewed the wartime contributions of the Yue dating back to Emperor Gao's era. It was noted that Yao, the lord of Min, had distinguished himself through exceptional service and commanded the loyal devotion of his people. He was therefore made the King of the Eastern Sea, with his capital at Dong'ou—and so the people came to call him the King of Dong'ou.

sentences.zh: 後數世，至孝景三年，吳王濞反，欲從閩越，閩越未肯行，獨東甌從吳。

translations.literal: Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing, King Bi of Wu rebelled and sought to enlist Minyue, but Minyue refused to go along; only Dong'ou joined Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, King Bi of Wu launched his rebellion and tried to recruit the Minyue to his cause, but they refused. Only Dong'ou chose to side with Wu.

sentences.zh: 及吳破，東甌受漢購，殺吳王丹徒，以故皆得不誅，歸國。

translations.literal: When Wu was defeated, Dong'ou accepted Han's bounty and killed the King of Wu at Dantu, and for this reason all were spared execution and returned to their kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, Dong'ou accepted a bounty from the Han court and killed the King of Wu at Dantu. For this reason they were all spared punishment and allowed to return to their kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 吳王子子駒亡走閩越，怨東甌殺其父，常勸閩越擊東甌。

translations.literal: The son of the King of Wu, Ziju, fled to Minyue, bore a grudge against Dong'ou for killing his father, and constantly urged Minyue to attack Dong'ou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziju, the prince of Wu, fled to Minyue. Harboring a deep resentment against Dong'ou for slaying his father, he constantly urged the Minyue to attack them.

sentences.zh: 至建元三年，閩越發兵圍東甌。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Jianyuan era, Minyue dispatched troops to besiege Dong'ou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianyuan era, the Minyue sent their army to lay siege to Dong'ou.

sentences.zh: 東甌食盡，困，且降，乃使人告急天子。

translations.literal: Dong'ou's food supplies were exhausted, they were in dire straits, and on the verge of surrender, so they sent envoys to urgently appeal to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'ou's provisions ran out. Desperate and on the brink of surrender, they dispatched envoys to make an urgent appeal to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子問太尉田蚡，蚡對曰：「越人相攻擊，固其常，又數反覆，不足以煩中國往救也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven consulted Grand Commandant Tian Fen. Fen replied: 'The Yue people attacking each other is simply their custom; moreover, they have been fickle time and again, so it is not worth troubling the Middle Kingdom to go rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Grand Commandant Tian Fen, who replied: 'The Yue attacking one another is simply their custom. They have been fickle time and again, and it is hardly worth troubling the Middle Kingdom to send troops to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 自秦時棄弗屬。」

translations.literal: Since the time of Qin, they have been abandoned and not governed.'
translations.idiomatic: They have been beyond our domain since the days of Qin.'

sentences.zh: 於是中大夫莊助詰蚡曰：「特患力弗能救，德弗能覆；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Palace Grandee Zhuang Zhu challenged Fen, saying: 'One would only worry that our strength might be insufficient to rescue them or our virtue insufficient to shelter them;
translations.idiomatic: At this, the Palace Grandee Zhuang Zhu confronted Fen, saying: 'The only question is whether we lack the strength to rescue them or the virtue to shelter them;

sentences.zh: 誠能，何故棄之？

translations.literal: If we truly are able, why then abandon them?
translations.idiomatic: If we truly have the power, why should we abandon them?

sentences.zh: 且秦舉咸陽而棄之，何乃越也！

translations.literal: Moreover, Qin abandoned even Xianyang itself—how much less should we fuss about Yue!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Qin abandoned even Xianyang itself—how much less should we trouble ourselves over Yue!

sentences.zh: 今小國以窮困來告急天子，天子弗振，彼當安所告愬？

translations.literal: Now a small kingdom comes in desperation to urgently appeal to the Son of Heaven; if the Son of Heaven does not come to its aid, where else shall they turn to plead their case?
translations.idiomatic: Now a small kingdom, driven to desperation, has come to plead with the emperor. If the emperor refuses to act, where else are they to turn?

sentences.zh: 又何以子萬國乎？」

translations.literal: And how then can we serve as parent to the ten thousand kingdoms?'
translations.idiomatic: And how then can we claim to be a parent to the myriad kingdoms?'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「太尉未足與計。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The Grand Commandant is not one to plan with.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'The Grand Commandant is not fit to be consulted on this matter.

sentences.zh: 吾初即位，不欲出虎符發兵郡國。」

translations.literal: I have only just ascended the throne and do not wish to issue tiger tallies to mobilize troops from the commanderies and kingdoms.'
translations.idiomatic: I have only just come to the throne, and I am reluctant to issue the tiger tallies to mobilize the armies of the commanderies and kingdoms.'

sentences.zh: 乃遣莊助以節發兵會稽。

translations.literal: Then he dispatched Zhuang Zhu with the imperial credentials to mobilize troops from Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Zhuang Zhu with an imperial tally to raise troops from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守欲距不為發兵，助乃斬一司馬，諭意指，遂發兵浮海救東甌。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator of Kuaiji wanted to refuse and would not dispatch troops, but Zhu then executed one colonel, made his intentions clear, and thereupon mobilized the troops to sail across the sea and rescue Dong'ou.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator of Kuaiji tried to obstruct the mobilization, but Zhu executed one of his colonels to demonstrate his authority, and the troops were duly dispatched across the sea to relieve Dong'ou.

sentences.zh: 未至，閩越引兵而去。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Minyue withdrew its troops and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the relief force even arrived, the Minyue pulled back their troops and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 東甌請舉國徙中國，乃悉舉眾來，處江淮之閒。

translations.literal: Dong'ou requested to relocate the entire kingdom to the interior, so they moved all their people and settled between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'ou petitioned to relocate their entire kingdom to the interior. They moved all their people and resettled in the lands between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.

sentences.zh: 至建元六年，閩越擊南越。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Jianyuan era, Minyue attacked Nanyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Jianyuan era, the Minyue launched an attack on Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 南越守天子約，不敢擅發兵擊而以聞。

translations.literal: Nanyue observed the Son of Heaven's covenant and did not dare to send troops on its own to counterattack, but instead reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyue honored its covenant with the emperor and refrained from retaliating on its own, choosing instead to report the aggression to the court.

sentences.zh: 上遣大行王恢出豫章，大農韓安國出會稽，皆為將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the Grand Herald Wang Hui from Yuzhang and the Grand Minister of Agriculture Han Anguo from Kuaiji, both serving as generals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Grand Herald Wang Hui forth from Yuzhang and the Grand Minister of Agriculture Han Anguo from Kuaiji, each to serve as a commanding general.

sentences.zh: 兵未踰嶺，閩越王郢發兵距險。

translations.literal: Before the troops had crossed the mountain ranges, the King of Minyue, Ying, dispatched troops to hold the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Han armies had even crossed the mountain passes, King Ying of Minyue sent his own troops to fortify the defiles.

sentences.zh: 其弟餘善乃與相、宗族謀曰：「王以擅發兵擊南越，不請，故天子兵來誅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu Shan then plotted with the chancellor and the clansmen, saying: 'The king launched an unauthorized attack on Nanyue without requesting permission, so the Son of Heaven's troops have come to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Yu Shan, conspired with the chancellor and their kinsmen, saying: 'The king attacked Nanyue without imperial permission, and that is why the emperor's armies have come to punish him.

sentences.zh: 今漢兵眾彊，今即幸勝之，后來益多，終滅國而止。

translations.literal: Now the Han troops are numerous and strong; even if we are fortunate enough to defeat them now, more will come later, and it will only end with the destruction of our kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The Han armies are vast and powerful. Even if we were lucky enough to repel them today, they would only send more, and in the end our kingdom would be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今殺王以謝天子。

translations.literal: Let us now kill the king to apologize to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Let us kill the king and apologize to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子聽，罷兵，固一國完；

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven accepts, he will withdraw the troops, and surely the kingdom will be preserved intact;
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor accepts, he will withdraw his forces, and the kingdom can be preserved;

sentences.zh: 不聽，乃力戰；

translations.literal: If he does not accept, then we fight with all our strength;
translations.idiomatic: If he does not, then we fight with everything we have;

sentences.zh: 不勝，即亡入海。」

translations.literal: If we cannot win, then we flee into the sea.'
translations.idiomatic: And if we cannot prevail, we flee to the sea.'

sentences.zh: 皆曰「善」。

translations.literal: All said: 'Agreed.'
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 即鏦殺王，使使奉其頭致大行。

translations.literal: They then assassinated the king with a lance and sent an envoy to present his head to the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: They struck the king down and sent an envoy to deliver his head to the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 大行曰：「所為來者誅王。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald said: 'The reason we came was to execute the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald declared: 'Our purpose in coming was to punish the king.

sentences.zh: 今王頭至，謝罪，不戰而耘，利莫大焉。」

translations.literal: Now the king's head has arrived, they have apologized for their crimes, and we achieve our aim without battle—there is no greater advantage than this.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that the king's head has been delivered, and they have submitted, we reap the harvest without shedding a drop of blood—there is no greater advantage.'

sentences.zh: 乃以便宜案兵告大農軍，而使使奉王頭馳報天子。

translations.literal: He then, acting on his own discretion, halted the troops and informed the Grand Minister of Agriculture's army, while sending an envoy to present the king's head and gallop to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on his own authority, he halted the advance and notified the army of the Grand Minister of Agriculture, while dispatching a rider to present the king's head to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔罷兩將兵，曰：「郢等首惡，獨無諸孫繇君丑不與謀焉。」

translations.literal: An edict dismissed both generals' troops, stating: 'Ying and the others were the principal offenders; only Chou, Lord Yao, the grandson of Wuzhu, did not participate in the conspiracy.'
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict ordered both armies to stand down, declaring: 'Ying and his accomplices were the chief culprits. Only Chou, Lord Yao, a grandson of Wuzhu, had no part in the conspiracy.'

sentences.zh: 乃使郎中將立丑為越繇王，奉閩越先祭祀。

translations.literal: Then a Palace Gentleman was sent to establish Chou as King of Yueyao, to maintain the ancestral sacrifices of Minyue.
translations.idiomatic: A Palace Gentleman-General was then dispatched to install Chou as the King of Yueyao, charged with maintaining the ancestral rites of the Minyue.

sentences.zh: 餘善已殺郢，威行於國，國民多屬，竊自立為王。

translations.literal: After Yu Shan had killed Ying, his authority prevailed throughout the kingdom, many of the people attached themselves to him, and he secretly declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Ying, Yu Shan's authority spread across the land. The people rallied to him in great numbers, and he secretly proclaimed himself king.

sentences.zh: 繇王不能矯其眾持正。

translations.literal: The King of Yao was unable to correct his people and maintain proper order.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Yao could not correct his people and uphold proper order.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之，為餘善不足復興師，曰：「餘善數與郢謀亂，而後首誅郢，師得不勞。」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of this, he deemed it not worth raising troops again over Yu Shan, saying: 'Yu Shan repeatedly plotted rebellion with Ying, but then was the first to execute Ying, so the troops were spared their labor.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he decided it was not worth mobilizing the army again on account of Yu Shan, remarking: 'Yu Shan plotted rebellion alongside Ying time and again, yet in the end he was the first to bring Ying to justice, sparing our forces the trouble.'

sentences.zh: 因立餘善為東越王，與繇王并處。

translations.literal: Therefore, Yu Shan was established as the King of Dongyue, dwelling alongside the King of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: And so Yu Shan was made the King of Dongyue, to rule alongside the King of Yao.

sentences.zh: 至元鼎五年，南越反，東越王餘善上書，請以卒八千人從樓船將軍擊呂嘉等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanding era, Nanyue rebelled, and the King of Dongyue, Yu Shan, submitted a memorial requesting to lead eight thousand soldiers to follow the General of the Towered Ships in attacking Lu Jia and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yuanding era, when Nanyue rebelled, Yu Shan, the King of Dongyue, submitted a petition offering to lead eight thousand troops to join the General of the Towered Ships in the campaign against Lu Jia and his allies.

sentences.zh: 兵至揭揚，以海風波為解，不行，持兩端，陰使南越。

translations.literal: When his troops reached Jieyang, he used rough seas and storms as an excuse not to advance, played both sides, and secretly communicated with Nanyue.
translations.idiomatic: When his forces reached Jieyang, he used the stormy seas as a pretext to halt his advance. He played both sides, secretly sending envoys to Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 及漢破番禺，不至。

translations.literal: When Han defeated Panyu, he had still not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Han forces took Panyu, he had still not appeared.

sentences.zh: 是時樓船將軍楊仆使使上書，願便引兵擊東越。

translations.literal: At that time, the General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, sent an envoy to submit a memorial, requesting permission to conveniently lead his troops to attack Dongyue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, sent a memorial to the throne requesting permission to turn his forces against Dongyue.

sentences.zh: 上曰士卒勞倦，不許，罷兵，令諸校屯豫章梅領待命。

translations.literal: The emperor said the soldiers were weary and exhausted, did not permit it, dismissed the troops, and ordered the various officers to encamp at Meiling in Yuzhang to await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, saying the troops were weary from their campaigns, denied the request. He ordered the army to stand down and the officers to encamp at Meiling in Yuzhang to await further orders.

sentences.zh: 元鼎六年秋，餘善聞樓船請誅之，漢兵臨境，且往，乃遂反，發兵距漢道。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan heard that the General of the Towered Ships had requested to execute him and that Han troops were approaching the border and about to advance, so he rebelled and sent troops to block the Han routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year of the Yuanding era, Yu Shan learned that the General of the Towered Ships had petitioned for his execution and that Han forces were massing on the border. He rose in open rebellion, sending his troops to block the roads leading into his territory.

sentences.zh: 號將軍騶力等為「吞漢將軍」，入白沙、武林、梅嶺，殺漢三校尉。

translations.literal: He titled generals Zou Li and others as 'Han-Devouring Generals,' invaded Baisha, Wulin, and Meiling, and killed three Han colonels.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his general Zou Li and others the title of 'Han-Devouring Generals,' then launched attacks on Baisha, Wulin, and Meiling, killing three Han colonels.

sentences.zh: 是時漢使大農張成、故山州侯齒將屯，弗敢擊，卻就便處，皆坐畏懦誅。

translations.literal: At that time, the Han had sent the Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Cheng and the former Marquis of Shanzhou, Chi, to command the encampments, but they did not dare to attack, retreated to convenient positions, and were all executed for cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the Han court had placed the Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Cheng and the former Marquis of Shanzhou, Chi, in command of the garrisons, but neither dared engage the enemy. They withdrew to safer positions, and both were later executed for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 餘善刻「武帝」璽自立，詐其民，為妄言。

translations.literal: Yu Shan carved an imperial seal inscribed 'Martial Emperor' and proclaimed himself sovereign, deceiving his people with false pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shan had an imperial seal carved bearing the title 'Martial Emperor' and declared himself sovereign, deceiving his people with extravagant claims.

sentences.zh: 天子遣橫海將軍韓說出句章，浮海從東方往；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched the General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, from Gouzhang to sail across the sea and approach from the east;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, from Gouzhang to sail across the sea and approach from the east;

sentences.zh: 樓船將軍楊仆出武林；

translations.literal: The General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, set out from Wulin;
translations.idiomatic: The General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, marched from Wulin;

sentences.zh: 中尉王溫舒出梅嶺；

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Capital, Wang Wenshu, set out from Meiling;
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Capital, Wang Wenshu, advanced from Meiling;

sentences.zh: 越侯為戈船、下瀨將軍，出若邪、白沙。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yue served as the General of the Spear Boats and Rapids, setting out from Ruoye and Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Yue, appointed as the General of Spear Boats and Rapids, set out from Ruoye and Baisha.

sentences.zh: 元封元年冬，咸入東越。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of the Yuanfeng era, they all entered Dongyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of the Yuanfeng era, all the forces converged on Dongyue.

sentences.zh: 東越素發兵距險，使徇北將軍守武林，敗樓船軍數校尉，殺長吏。

translations.literal: Dongyue had already sent troops to block the defiles, assigning the General Who Patrols the North to defend Wulin; he defeated several colonels of the Towered Ships army and killed their senior officers.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyue had already dispatched forces to hold the mountain passes, placing the General Who Patrols the North at Wulin. He routed several colonels of the Towered Ships army and killed their commanding officers.

sentences.zh: 樓船將軍率錢唐轅終古斬徇北將軍，為御兒侯。

translations.literal: The General of the Towered Ships led the Qiantang garrison commander Yuan Zhonggu to behead the General Who Patrols the North, and Yuan Zhonggu was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yu'er.
translations.idiomatic: The General of the Towered Ships directed Yuan Zhonggu, the garrison commander of Qiantang, to slay the General Who Patrols the North. For this feat, Yuan Zhonggu was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yu'er.

sentences.zh: 自兵未往。

translations.literal: His own troops had not yet advanced.
translations.idiomatic: His main force, however, had yet to move forward.

sentences.zh: 故越衍侯吳陽前在漢，漢使歸諭餘善，餘善弗聽。

translations.literal: The former Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, had previously been in Han territory; Han sent him back to persuade Yu Shan, but Yu Shan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The former Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, had been residing at the Han court. The Han sent him back to reason with Yu Shan, but Yu Shan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 及橫海將軍先至，越衍侯吳陽以其邑七百人反，攻越軍於漢陽。

translations.literal: When the General Who Crosses the Sea arrived first, the Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, rebelled with seven hundred men from his fief and attacked the Yue army at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the General Who Crosses the Sea was the first to arrive, the Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, turned against Yu Shan with seven hundred men from his estate and attacked the Yue army at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 從建成侯敖，與其率，從繇王居股謀曰：「餘善首惡，劫守吾屬。

translations.literal: Together with the Marquis of Jiancheng, Ao, and his officers, and with the King of Yao, Ju Gu, they plotted, saying: 'Yu Shan is the chief offender; he has coerced and detained us and our dependents.
translations.idiomatic: He joined with the Marquis of Jiancheng, Ao, and his officers, and together with the King of Yao, Ju Gu, they plotted, saying: 'Yu Shan is the chief offender; he has coerced and detained us and our dependents.

sentences.zh: 今漢兵至，眾彊，計殺餘善，自歸諸將，儻幸得脫。」

translations.literal: Now the Han troops have arrived, numerous and strong; let us plan to kill Yu Shan, surrender ourselves to the various generals, and perhaps we may be fortunate enough to escape.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Han armies have come in force, let us kill Yu Shan and surrender to the Han generals—perhaps we will be fortunate enough to save ourselves.'

sentences.zh: 乃遂俱殺餘善，以其眾降橫海將軍，故封繇王居股為東成侯，萬戶；

translations.literal: They then together killed Yu Shan and surrendered their forces to the General Who Crosses the Sea; therefore the King of Yao, Ju Gu, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Dongcheng, with ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: They killed Yu Shan and surrendered their forces to the General Who Crosses the Sea. For this, the King of Yao, Ju Gu, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Dongcheng with a fief of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 封建成侯敖為開陵侯；

translations.literal: The Marquis of Jiancheng, Ao, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Kailing;
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Jiancheng, Ao, was made the Marquis of Kailing;

sentences.zh: 封越衍侯吳陽為北石侯；

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Beishi;
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Yueyan, Wu Yang, was made the Marquis of Beishi;

sentences.zh: 封橫海將軍說為案道侯；

translations.literal: The General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Andao;
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, was made the Marquis of Andao;

sentences.zh: 封橫海校尉福為繚嫈侯。

translations.literal: The Colonel Who Crosses the Sea, Fu, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Liaoying.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel Who Crosses the Sea, Fu, was made the Marquis of Liaoying.

sentences.zh: 福者，成陽共王子，故為海常侯，坐法失侯。

translations.literal: Fu was a son of King Gong of Chengyang, formerly the Marquis of Haichang, who lost his marquisate for violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a son of King Gong of Chengyang. He had previously held the title of Marquis of Haichang but lost it after running afoul of the law.

sentences.zh: 舊從軍無功，以宗室故侯。

translations.literal: He had previously served in the army without merit, but was made a marquis because of his imperial clan status.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had served in earlier campaigns without distinction, he was granted a marquisate on account of his imperial lineage.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆無成功，莫封。

translations.literal: The various generals all had no successful achievements, and none were enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: None of the other generals achieved any notable success, and so none received enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 東越將多軍，漢兵至，棄其軍降，封為無錫侯。

translations.literal: The Dongyue general Duo Jun, when the Han troops arrived, abandoned his army and surrendered, and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongyue general Duo Jun abandoned his forces and surrendered when the Han troops arrived. He was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 於是天子曰東越狹多阻，閩越悍，數反覆，詔軍吏皆將其民徙處江淮閒。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven declared that Dongyue was narrow and full of obstacles, Minyue fierce and repeatedly fickle, and decreed that the military officials should all lead the people to relocate between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then declared that Dongyue was narrow and full of barriers, that Minyue was fierce, and that they were repeatedly fickle. He decreed that the military officers were all to relocate their people to settle between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.

sentences.zh: 東越地遂虛。

translations.literal: The lands of Dongyue were thus emptied.
translations.idiomatic: And so the lands of Dongyue were left desolate.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：越雖蠻夷，其先豈嘗有大功德於民哉，何其久也！

translations.literal: The Grand Historian remarks: Though the Yue were barbarians, did their ancestors not once render great merit and virtue to the people? How enduring they were!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: Though the Yue were counted among the barbarian peoples, their ancestors must surely have bestowed great merit and virtue upon their people—how else could their line have endured so long!

sentences.zh: 歷數代常為君王，句踐一稱伯。

translations.literal: Through several generations they constantly served as kings and rulers, with Goujian once styling himself hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: For generation after generation they served as kings and rulers, and Goujian himself once rose to the rank of hegemon.

sentences.zh: 然餘善至大逆，滅國遷眾，其先苗裔繇王居股等猶尚封為萬戶侯，由此知越世世為公侯矣。

translations.literal: Yet though Yu Shan committed the greatest treason and the kingdom was destroyed and its people relocated, their ancestral descendants such as the King of Yao, Ju Gu, were still enfeoffed as marquises with ten thousand households; from this we know that the Yue served as dukes and marquises generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Yu Shan committed the greatest treason, destroying the kingdom and relocating its people, descendants of the royal line such as the King of Yao, Ju Gu, were still enfeoffed as marquises with ten thousand households. From this we know that the Yue generation after generation held the rank of duke or marquis.

sentences.zh: 蓋禹之餘烈也。

translations.literal: This was surely the lingering influence of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was the enduring legacy of the Great Yu.
